newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen hinging on Moody's, economic data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen hinging on Moody's, economic data.

text.p: The outlook for Thai stocks hinges on whether Moody's Investor Service downgrades the country's long-term debt rating and on key central bank economic indicators expected this week, analysts said on Wednesday.
The bloodied stock market made up some lost ground last week after the government and central bank quashed rumours of a baht devaluation and as pressure from a firm dollar eased, brokers said.
Moody's said on February 14 that it had placed Thailand's A2 foreign-currency sovereign ceilings for bonds and bank deposits on review for a possible downgrade.
The agency is sending two representatives to Bangkok next month. "Moody's upcoming recommendation poses a major concern to investors now," said Songyos Kulvichien, vice president of Securities One.
He saw strong support for the SET stock index at the 700-point level and said it had a good chance of advancing to 800 if Moody's did not downgrade the ratings.
The central bank releases the economic data on Thursday and investors will be watching out for the trade and current account deficit figures for December, analysts told Reuters.
Any narrowing of the deficits would bring cheer to the market, they said. The November trade deficit was 24 billion baht.

The stock index plunged to a 56-month low of 698.06 on February 13 as foreigners fled on concerns about the baht and worries about loan problems for financial institutions exposed to the ailing property sector.
The index was down 12.73 points at 727.02 at the midday break on Wednesday.
High interest rates, in place to deter currency speculators who have launched raids on the baht since late last year, were also seen hurting the stock market and inhibiting liquidity, analysts said.
Busaba Kunasirin, analyst at Chao Phya Finance and Securities, believed the index could rise to the 800 in the near term as bargain hunters were already returning.
"The market P/E (price earnings ratio) now stands at 10.76 which is very low compared to 31.49 times on January 4, 1994, when the index hit its peak," Busaba said.
She said several listed firms, such as those in the entertainment and energy sectors, were still performing well in terms of net profit growth.

Thai bank shares with cheap valuations were set to bounce back once interest rates fell and investors were confident the central bank had successfully beaten back attacks on the baht, Asset Plus Securities said this week.
